tasks.title: Read a thousands separator
tasks.statement: Parse the number with the comma removed and print it.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO

df = pd.read_csv(StringIO("v\n1,200\n"), thousands=",")
print(df["v"].tolist())

tasks.title: JSON split keys
tasks.statement: Serialise with the split orient and print the sorted top-level keys.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"a": [1]})
import json
print(sorted(json.loads(df.to_json(orient="split")).keys()))

tasks.title: Skip comment lines
tasks.statement: Read the file ignoring comment lines and print the row count.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO

text = "# note\na\n1\n# other\n2"

tasks.title: Keep the zip as text

tasks.solution:

tasks.title: Merge on two keys
tasks.statement: Merge on id and year and print the row count.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1], "year": [2025, 2026]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1, 1], "year": [2025, 2026]})
print(len(a.merge(b, on=["id", "year"])))

tasks.title: Join on the index
tasks.statement: Join the two frames on their indexes and print the columns.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1]}, index=["k"])
b = pd.DataFrame({"y": [2]}, index=["k"])
print(a.join(b).columns.tolist())

tasks.title: Concat with keys
tasks.statement: Concatenate with keys and print the index level names.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"x": [1]})
print(pd.concat([a, a], keys=["p", "q"]).index.names)

tasks.title: Collision suffixes
tasks.statement: Merge with the suffixes _l and _r and print the column names.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

a = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "v": [1]})
b = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "v": [2]})
print(a.merge(b, on="id", suffixes=("_l", "_r")).columns.tolist())

tasks.title: Count by two keys
tasks.statement: Count rows per city and year and print the shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Pune", "Delhi"], "year": [2026, 2026, 2026]})
print(df.groupby(["city", "year"]).size().shape)

tasks.title: Running total inside a group

tasks.solution:

df = pd.DataFrame({"g": ["a", "a", "b"], "v": [1, 2, 3]})
print(df.groupby("g")["v"].cumsum().tolist())

tasks.title: Pivot with a count
tasks.statement: Cross city and year counting rows, and print the shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune", "Pune"], "year": [2026, 2026]})
print(df.pivot_table(index="city", columns="year", values="city", aggfunc="count").shape)

tasks.title: Unstack a groupby
tasks.statement: Group by two keys and print the unstacked shape.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"city": ["Pune"], "year": [2026], "v": [1]})
print(df.groupby(["city", "year"])["v"].sum().unstack().shape)

tasks.title: Melt and pivot back
tasks.statement: Melt the frame, pivot it back and print the recovered value.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

df = pd.DataFrame({"id": [1], "a": [3]})
long = pd.melt(df, id_vars="id")
wide = long.pivot(index="id", columns="variable", values="value")
print(int(wide["a"].iloc[0]))

tasks.title: Two aggregations per month
tasks.statement: Resample to month starts and print the sum and count.
tasks.solution:
import pandas as pd

s = pd.Series([1, 2], index=pd.to_datetime(["2026-01-01", "2026-01-02"]))
out = s.resample("MS").agg(["sum", "count"])
print(out.values.tolist())

tasks.title: Rolling with one observation
